success_patterns: Bare work title plus year ('"Rachel, Rachel"(1968)'): the agent answered with the creator (director Paul Newman), the person the passages repeatedly pair with the title ('directed by'). It did not answer with the title or a plot detail.

Fragment clue with a leading ellipsis ('...as the U.S. holiday Decoration Day'): the agent answered with the other name of the thing, which is the entity the passages say was 'originally called Decoration Day'. It did not answer with a description.

A passage reproduced the clue verbatim with a trivia-news or archive answer ('The clue: ... "What is France?"', 'sitcom taught us ... | Welcome Back, Kotter'). The agent copied the answer, dropping the 'What is' wrapper.

Clues with 'this/these' plus category words were answered with the category referent in the form the passages use ('these people born between '46 & '64' -> 'baby boomers'; 'this creator of Uncle Remus' -> Joel Chandler Harris). Each answer was confirmed by several passages repeating the clue's details.
Clues whose wording closely matched a sentence in many passages (Outsiders, Jesse Owens, Monaco/France) were answered by taking the entity that co-occurs with all the clue's distinctive details.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers verbatim archive hits and referent slot-typing. Three recurring successful behaviours are not stated explicitly. (1) A clue that is only a work's title and year wants its creator. (2) A leading-ellipsis fragment about an alias or former name wants the current or other name. (3) An archive or news answer written as a 'What is X?' / 'Who is X' response should be copied with that wrapper stripped. These edits are short and reinforce existing sections without the broad rewrites that were rejected earlier.

edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.
edits.content:
- A clue that is only a work's title, often with a year (e.g. '"Rachel, Rachel"(1968)'), asks for the work's creator: the director of a film, the author of a book, the composer of a piece. Pick the person that most passages pair with the title ('directed by X', 'novel by X'). Do not answer with the title itself or a plot detail.
- A fragment such as '...as the U.S. holiday Decoration Day' or '...also known as X' is the tail of a sentence about an alias or former name. Answer with the other name that the passages tie to X ('originally called Decoration Day' -> 'Memorial Day').

edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.
edits.content: - An answer printed as a Jeopardy-style response ('The clue: ... "What is France?"', 'Who is Jesse Owens?') counts as a verbatim hit. Copy only the entity and drop 'What is' / 'Who is'. This applies even when the snippet comes from a news or game-show recap rather than an archive page. Treat only the contestant's WRONG responses as noise.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - When the clue defines a group by description ('these people born between '46 & '64', 'these fish'), answer with the common name for that group as the passages phrase it ('baby boomers'), not the date range or an example member.
